title: Prefix-scoped deterministic eviction with auditability under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem statement: As continuous batching and KV caching scale across GPU shards, existing heuristics (LRU, TTL) produce nondeterministic eviction behavior when multiple concurrent batches and namespace-prefix pinning interact. This leads to rare but reproducible correctness issues: stale prefix hits, accidental prefix cross-contamination, and transient failures when cached KV slices referenced by in-flight batched requests are reclaimed mid-serve. We need a deterministic, prefix-scoped eviction policy with an auditable tombstone trail that provides correctness guarantees under concurrent serving and enables safe reclaiming of GPU memory with minimal tail-latency impact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic eviction ordering for prefix-scoped keys: given identical request history, eviction decisions are reproducible across restarts and replicas.
- No request must fail or return stale KV entries because of eviction while in-flight; batched requests referencing a cached prefix must either succeed with the previously associated KV state or the runtime must transparently fallback to a compatible model variant.
- Audit trail: every eviction must emit a lightweight tombstone event containing prefix, key-hash, epoch, and reclaimable-at timestamp written to the observability pipeline. Events must be queryable in Console and show up in the per-route trace.
- Overhead: per-key metadata increase must not exceed 16 bytes on average, and eviction path must not add >5% median CPU for the runtime under typical loads.
- End-to-end tests must simulate concurrent continuous batching and demonstrate zero correctness regressions over 10k randomized scenarios.
implementation_notes: Design summary: Implement an epoch-based deterministic eviction coordinator that combines three signals: prefix-weighted LRU rank, TTL, and a pinning layer for active batches. Key concepts: 1) Epochs: periodic monotonic epoch counter incremented on choke points (shard restarts, config changes) used to timestamp cache inserts/refreshes. 2) Tombstones: when a key is evicted, we record a tombstone with (prefix, key-hash, epoch, reclaimable_at). Tombstones are retained for the maximum in-flight request window + safety_margin. 3) Pinning semantics: a batch acquires prefix-scoped pins (not per-key) at batch start; pins prevent eviction of keys with matching prefix and epoch <= pin_epoch. 4) Deterministic order: eviction selection sorts candidate keys by (prefix-priority, last_access_epoch, ttl_expiry, lru_position) using stable, shard-consistent sort; ties broken by key-hash to guarantee determinism across replicas. 5) Audit stream: tombstones and pin events are emit-only, idempotent and buffered to observability with a small backpressure budget.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Metadata and tombstone retention adds memory overhead and slightly increases GC churn; mitigated by compact encoding and a configurable retention window.
- Determinism can make eviction less reactive to sudden workload changes compared to pure LRU; we offset with configurable prefix-weight adjustments and emergency reclaim heuristics.
- Complexity increases in pinning logic may introduce subtle deadlocks if not carefully designed; thorough unit testing and formal invariants check required.
- If tombstone pipeline is down, we must still guarantee correctness: eviction must fall back to local retention policy and postpone reclaim until observability backlog drains. This is acceptable as a temporary degraded mode.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: pin acquisition/release invariants, tombstone encoding/decoding, stable sorting equivalence classes.
- Integration tests: multi-shard simulator that runs continuous batching workload generator with configurable prefix distributions; verify deterministic eviction ordering by replaying same seed across replicas.
- Chaos tests: kill/restart shards and scheduler, verify correctness with in-flight batches and tombstone recovery.
- Performance benchmarks: measure per-key metadata overhead, median CPU increase, and end-to-end latency impact under 95th/99th percentile loads.
- Regression suite: extend existing KV correctness harness to add 10k randomized scenarios where TTL/LRU/prefix skew vary; expected zero correctness failures.
- E2E canary: enable feature flag in staging for a small number of routes for 48h with strict tracing and alerting on trace-level mismatches.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged implementation behind runtime flag 'deterministic_prefix_eviction'. 2) Nightly staging runs with simulator for 72h to collect traces and tombstones. 3) Canary: enable on 5% of hosted routes with routes that have low customer impact and with increased tracing. 4) If stable, ramp to Dedicated customers with explicit opt-in, collect telemetry for 7 days. 5) Gradual global rollout over two weeks with rollback flag.
Fallbacks: immediate toggle to legacy eviction policy; tombstone ingestion failures auto-disable audit emission but preserve correctness by increasing retention.
implementation_steps:
- Phase 1 (API & metadata): Add epoch counter to shard metadata, extend per-key header to include last_access_epoch and small prefix-id.
- Phase 2 (pinning): Implement prefix-scoped pin acquisition API integrated with batch lifecycle; add pin expiration guard.
- Phase 3 (eviction coordinator): Implement deterministic selection sort and tombstone emitter; wire to existing reclaim path.
- Phase 4 (observability): Add tombstone consumer in Console and per-route trace hooks.
- Phase 5 (tests & canary): Run aforementioned testing plan and iterate on throttle/retention settings.
comments: 2025-01-16 Aisha Raman: Initial write-up; submitting for architecture review. Added project link to KV Cache Consistency initiative.

2025-01-20 Priya Shah (review): We should ensure tombstones cannot be forged by misbehaving shards; suggested signing tombstone events or including shard id + epoch to trace. Also requested a bounded queue mechanism for observability emission.

2025-01-28 Ethan Cole (review): Concerned about prefix pin explosion if many small batches acquire pins; suggest prefix coalescing and maximum concurrent pin limit per prefix. Also suggested simulating pathological prefix fanout in chaos tests.

2025-02-05 Luca Moreno: Implemented epoch counter and per-key header. Added compact encoding to limit metadata to 12 bytes average in local tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2413
2025-02-12 QA: Ran deterministic replay harness for 1k seeds; saw one mismatch traced to a race in pin release during batch retry — fixed in PR 2421.
